title.value: [MS2] A project description does not resolve object references the way an issue's does

body.value:
**Found while checking whether the project description was missing anything the issue description has (2026-09-02).** It was, but not rendering — RIC-6 gave both surfaces that.

The asymmetry is PRO-7's behaviour, present on one and absent on the other.

| | `IssueView` | `ProjectHeader` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nostr:naddr…` stripped from the prose | yes, `stripNaddrs(description)` | **no** |
| the referenced object drawn below | yes, `<ForeignReferences>` | **no** |
| rich text rendered | yes | yes (ship#82) |

So a project description containing a reference shows the reader a wall of bech32 *and* nothing that says what it names — which is exactly the outcome PRO-7 removed from the issue surface, on the argument that the bech32 is the half that means nothing to a person.

## It is latent, not biting

Measured on production 2026-09-02: **0 project descriptions and 0 issue descriptions currently carry a `nostr:naddr`.** So nothing is broken on screen today, and this is not urgent.

It is still worth filing rather than leaving to be rediscovered: a project description is the field this whole project chose as its test bed, it is the longest body in the workspace, and the first person to paste a reference into one gets the pre-PRO-7 experience with no indication that the issue surface behaves differently.

## What to build

`ProjectHeader` does what `IssueView` does: `display`/`displayNode` over `stripNaddrs(description)`, and `<ForeignReferences text={description}>` below. Both already exist; this is wiring, not design.

Worth deciding while doing it whether the pairing belongs in one component rather than being assembled correctly twice — that is the shape of defect this is.

## Done when

A project description containing a `nostr:naddr…` renders without the bech32 in its prose and with the referenced object below it, matching the issue surface; and there is a test, because this gap existed with every suite green.

actions.label: Change status
actions.description: Move an issue through its lifecycle by setting its status to one of the issueStatuses values. The status is not on the issue — it lives on the change stream — so this is the only way to move it, and every move stays attributable to whoever made it.

actions.label: Assign
actions.description: Say who is doing an issue, by public key. An empty value clears the assignment. Distinct from a project lead, which is accountability for a whole project rather than for this one issue.

actions.label: Comment
actions.description: Say something about a project or an issue that is not a change to one of its fields. The comment lands in the Folder both apps read, so it appears in the paired conversation as well as on the object.
